event_name: Alse Young hanged — first American witch execution
significance: Alse (Alice) Young of Windsor, Connecticut, was hanged for witchcraft on May 26, 1647, making her the first person executed for witchcraft in British colonial America; her case preceded the Salem trials by forty-five years and was part of approximately eleven witch executions in Connecticut before 1663, demonstrating that colonial American witch prosecution was not a Salem-specific anomaly.
source_method: Connecticut colonial court records; analyzed in Norton, In the Devil's Snare (2002) and Demos, Entertaining Satan (1982)
